policies.title: Brunei: Category D1 ordinary-passport 90-day visa waiver
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Category D1, whose conditions expressly waive a visa for up to 90 days.
conditions: The D1 waiver is up to 90 days. A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; no work, residence, professional visit or extension right is established.

E-Arrival Card registration supplies arrival/travel/accommodation information and a reference number. Immigration separately requires a visa if applicable, so the declaration is not normalized as an ETA or visa authorization.
A recognised passport with at least six months’ validity is required. Admission, funds, onward travel, security, health and immigration-officer conditions remain separate.

policies.title: Brunei: Category D2 ordinary-passport 30-day visa waiver
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Category D2, whose conditions expressly waive a visa for up to 30 days.
conditions: The D2 waiver is up to 30 days. A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; no work, residence, professional visit or extension right is established.

The statutory Schedule 2 exemption is limited to entry by air through Brunei International Airport and requires the Controller to be satisfied of confirmed return or outward passage. This policy preserves that route and onward-travel condition.
E-Arrival Card registration is an arrival declaration, not an ETA or visa authorization; the Immigration guidance separately calls for a visa when applicable.

A recognised passport with at least six months’ validity, ordinary admission rules and individual officer assessment apply. Diplomatic, official, service and special-document arrangements are excluded.

policies.title: Brunei: Category D3 ordinary-passport 14-day visa waiver
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Category D3, whose conditions expressly waive a visa for up to 14 days.
conditions: The D3 waiver is up to 14 days. A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; no work, residence, professional visit or extension right is established.

The statutory Schedule 3 exemption remains subject to conditions the Controller of Immigration may impose. Kosovo is expressly added to that schedule by the 2026 Gazette amendment, and the current MFA schedule places its ordinary passport in D3.
E-Arrival Card registration is a declaration, not an ETA or visa authorization. A recognised passport with at least six months’ validity and individual admissibility conditions apply.

policies.title: Brunei: Category C1 ordinary-passport 30-day visa on arrival
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Category C1, whose conditions permit a visa-on-arrival application for 30 days.
conditions: C1 permits an application for single- or multiple-entry visa on arrival for 30 days, with the published BND20/BND30 fees and visa form/arrival-card procedure.

A visa application is required for a longer stay and for business visits; the arrival route does not establish work, residence, professional-visit, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document access.
E-Arrival Card registration is a declaration, not an ETA and not the visa-on-arrival itself. Passport validity, admission and all individual requirements remain applicable.

conditions: C2 permits a single-entry 14-day visa-on-arrival application, with the published BND20 fee and visa form/arrival-card procedure.

policies.title: Brunei: Category A and B ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: The live MFA country schedule assigns these ordinary passports to Categories A or B; both categories expressly require a visa through a Brunei mission abroad.
conditions: The assignment comes from the explicit, live MFA country-by-country Category A/B schedule—not from an unlisted-country complement. Both categories say a visa is required and may be applied for through the nearest Brunei mission abroad; the reviewed material does not establish an electronic alternative.

The FAQ distinguishes short/social, business and professional visit visas. Business and professional visits require a Brunei registered/government-linked sponsor application, and employment needs the appropriate visa and employment pass before arrival.

E-Arrival Card registration is an arrival declaration and does not replace the required visa. Transit is separately limited to a 72-hour transit pass with onward ticket and airline sponsor/guarantor; it is not normalized as a visitor route.

Valid recognised passport, six-month validity, fees, duration, entry count, documentary criteria and individual admissibility remain subject to the competent authorities. Diplomatic, official, service, residence and special-document arrangements are excluded.

unresolved.reason: The reviewed current Immigration material establishes that Brunei biometric passports are issued to Brunei citizens, but no directly applicable current official source was located that normalizes a Brunei ordinary-passport holder’s entry as the repository’s citizenship/right-of-entry status. Citizenship is therefore not inferred from foreign-national visa rules or passport issuance.
